title: Siouxland Chamber of Commerce hosts economic luncheon - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Prieto-Rivero Maren Ewertz ,
1 hours ago SIOUX CITY , Iowa ( KCAU ) — A luncheon, attended by high-level Siouxland executives, opened the door to questions for economic experts from all three Siouxland states.
“This represents an opportunity for our executive leadership to interface with one another,” said Chris McGowan with the Siouxland Chamber of Commerce.
The meeting featured three regional economic leaders: Professor of Economics at Creighton University, Dr. Ernie Goss; South Dakota Bureau of Finance & Management Commissioner Jim Terwilliger; and State Chief Economist for the Iowa Department of Revenue Robin Anderson.
Story continues below
“They have told us that a $40 trillion debt is something that we must begin to pay closer attention to,” said McGowan. “That needs to start right now.”
“What we’re seeing out there is some real volatility,” said Goff. “Some uncertainty because of tariffs, also AI (artificial intelligence), AI is creating uncertainty out there.”
A WalletHub report found all three states ranked in the bottom 15 among the states measured, including Washington, D.C.
KCAU 9 asked how each state can rebound from its low overall ranking.
“As agriculture rebounds, as manufacturing rebounds, you’re going to see that the three states will outgrow the rest of the U.S.,” said Goff.
“In South Dakota, we talk about looking to add value where we can,” said Terwilliger. “We talked a lot about value-added ag. Just south of Mitchell, we opened a soybean processing facility last fall, and that adds a lot of value in the ag sector.”
“We have seen a little bit of improvement in some manufacturing jobs,” said Anderson. “But there’s not enough to discern a trend yet. And I’ll be looking to see what kind of forecast comes out for net farm income out of the USDA for 2026.”
Although economies in the tri-state area rank low compared to most U.S. states, officials say growth is expected to continue its upward trend.
